title: Cell timing offsets created false negative links in positive models of two adult worm maps
abstract: We tested cell timing offsets in positive linear circuit models of two partial adult worm chemical maps with 180 common cells. A proof shows that a positive-lag covariance estimate preserves decay eigenvalues but can change link signs. At gain 0.8 and maximum cell delay of one assumed leak time, ten assigned delay vectors gave median weight errors of 45.41% and 43.39%. Negative estimates made up 7.97% and 7.09% of the strongest links selected at the known link count. An exact three-cell feedforward example produced a negative estimate for an absent direct link. Known timing removed the error at the population level by shifting each pair covariance to its correct lag. This requires covariance values beyond two fixed lag matrices. These are model results, not measured activity fits. Positive weights, assigned delays, full observation and two partial maps limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, external source hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Cell timing offsets change weight estimates and add negative selected links in two positive adult worm models. Lines are medians across ten assigned delay vectors; bands are full ranges. Gain is 0.8. These are population model results.
